title:
Office Automation
Readiness Brief
subtitle: A decision-ready view of the governed PowerPoint, Word and Excel runtime shipped by dcc-mcp-office.

decision.label: DECISION IN ONE MINUTE
decision.title: Adopt the shared Office core for governed desktop automation.
decision.body: The current runtime already covers editable deck generation, native document inspection, safe cross-file text replacement and validated PDF delivery. Every write remains confirmation-gated, checkpointed and independently verifiable.

capabilities.proof: Compile branded decks, inspect files, render slides, replace text and export PDF.
Inspect documents, replace body/header/footer text and export PDF.
Inspect workbooks, replace cell text and export native PDF.

workflow.name: Discover
workflow.body: Handshake with the application-specific sidecar and accept only its advertised office-rpc/1 capabilities.

workflow.name: Plan
workflow.body: Keep reusable JSON or document input separate from generated artifacts and choose the narrowest valid backend.

workflow.name: Preview
workflow.body: Run non-destructive inspection or dry-run first, then surface the exact files, matches and risk posture.

workflow.name: Confirm
workflow.body: Require explicit confirmation for destructive writes and capture a byte-exact checkpoint before mutation.

workflow.name: Verify
workflow.body: Re-open outputs, validate postconditions, render previews and record a sanitized audit transcript with checksums.

safeguards.title: Deny by default
safeguards.body: Macros, VBA, external links and arbitrary ExecuteMso paths are never silently relaxed.

safeguards.title: Application isolation
safeguards.body: PowerPoint, Word and Excel run behind separate per-application sidecars and COM lifecycles.

safeguards.title: Evidence over claims
safeguards.body: The gallery ships editable Office files, native exports, rendered previews, RPC transcripts and SHA-256 manifests.

boundary: Current evidence covers PowerPoint, Word and Excel desktop automation. Microsoft Graph and Office.js remain Phase 3; Visio, Project and Access remain future scope and are not represented as shipped capabilities.
